# `kernel/execution/DodadCommandIr.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/execution/DodadCommandIr.js`

Request-scoped command IR for granular Dodad authoring. Models emit short typed handles instead of revision authority, hashes, or raw operation paths. Human-readable paths may appear once as inert context; they never enter the executable program. This module validates the symbol table and deterministically compiles admitted commands into the existing granular update envelope. It performs no storage access, tool dispatch, or mutation.

## Functions

### `async normalizeDodadCommandScope(input = {})`

Validate and freeze the private request-local symbol table used by one command sequence. File contents and hashes remain local authority.

### `async normalizeDodadCommandIr(input = {}, { scope } = {})`

Validate one complete model-facing command program against its exact scope.

### `async compileDodadCommandIr(input = {}, { scope } = {})`

Compile a command program into the existing granular update envelope. The returned value includes the existing deterministic patch hash and grants no storage or tool authority.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
